subject: Animation
title: The Multiplane Camera
description: Learn The Multiplane Camera in one minute.

hook.text: In the 1930s, Disney built a camera that shot through stacked layers of painted glass.

buildup.text: Each glass layer held a different part of the scene — foreground, midground, and background.

discovery.text: By moving the layers at different speeds, the camera created a stunning illusion of depth.

twist.text: The device was enormous and expensive. Some shots took hours to set up for seconds of film.

climax.text: The multiplane camera debuted in The Old Mill and became essential to Disney's visual style.

punchline.text: Stacked glass gave flat drawings a third dimension.

quiz.question: What did Disney's multiplane camera achieve?
options: It added synchronized sound to cartoons
It created an illusion of depth by photographing through stacked painted glass layers
It allowed animators to draw directly onto film

details.summary: Disney's multiplane camera photographed animation artwork on multiple glass planes at different distances, creating genuine depth in 2D animation. First used in The Old Mill, this innovation gave Disney films a three-dimensional quality no competitor could match.
details.whyItMatters: The multiplane camera gave 2D animation the illusion of depth and parallax movement, dramatically increasing visual immersion. It solved a fundamental limitation of flat animation and remained essential until digital tools replaced it decades later.
takeaways: The multiplane camera photographed art on glass planes at different distances
It created depth and parallax effects impossible with single-plane photography
The technique was used from The Old Mill through The Little Mermaid

faq.question: How did the multiplane camera create depth?
faq.answer: Background elements were painted on glass planes at different distances from the camera. Moving the camera or the planes at different speeds created parallax — foreground objects moved faster than backgrounds, exactly as in real life. The result was convincing 3D depth in 2D art.

faq.question: How expensive was the multiplane camera?
faq.answer: The original camera cost approximately $70,000 in 1937 — equivalent to over a million dollars today. It stood over eleven feet tall and required a specially modified building. Only Disney could afford such an investment, giving the studio a massive visual advantage.
